001: I received an offer for a position with more responsibilities, but I don't know if I'm ready.
That's a great opportunity. What exactly is making you hesitate?
I'm afraid I won't measure up in front of the team.
You definitely have the skills to succeed, don't doubt yourself.
Thanks, it's reassuring to hear that from you.
Think it over calmly, but I think you should seize this chance.
002: I'd like to ask for a promotion, but I don't know how to go about it.
You should first prepare a solid file with your achievements.
I've already noted a few important projects, but I lack perspective.
You could also ask for a meeting with your manager to discuss it.
That's a good idea, I'll prepare a clear summary.
And above all, highlight your added value for the team.
003: My manager offered me a transfer abroad for two years.
That's an incredible opportunity for your career, don't you think?
Yes, but I have ties here and it scares me to leave everything behind.
That's understandable, but international experience is highly valued.
I know, and I've always dreamed of discovering another culture.
Maybe you could start with a short stay to get familiar with it.
004: I'm wondering if I should change fields to reinvent myself.
What's motivating you to consider this change?
I feel like I've seen everything there is to see in my current position.
That's a sign that you need new challenges, which is healthy.
But I'm afraid of losing what I've built and having to start from scratch.
Your skills are transferable, you'll know how to adapt.
005: I was selected for an internal mentoring program, it's a great source of pride.
Congratulations! That's an excellent opportunity to grow.
Yes, I'll be guided by an experienced female director.
That's perfect for expanding your network and refining your goals.
I hope it will help me clarify my professional plans.
Take advantage of this chance to ask all your questions without holding back.
006: I have to prepare my annual performance review, I'm a bit stressed.
Yet it's the perfect time to talk about your ambitions.
You're right, I'll prepare a list of my achievements and my wishes.
Don't forget to mention the training courses you'd like to take.
Yes, I'd like to get trained in project management.
That's a key skill, your manager should be receptive.
007: I turned down a very well-paid job offer, and now I'm having doubts.
Why did you turn it down if it was so appealing?
The company's values didn't match mine.
That's a brave decision, money isn't everything.
I tell myself I'll find an opportunity more aligned with my convictions.
And you'll be right, because fulfillment is essential in the long run.
008: My colleague got promoted instead of me, I feel a bit disappointed.
It's frustrating, but maybe it's just postponed.
I feel like my efforts aren't recognized enough.
Have you thought about talking about it openly with your manager?
Not yet, I don't want to seem demanding.
Expressing your expectations is legitimate, that's how you'll move forward.
009: I'm invited to an international conference to represent our team.
That's significant recognition of your expertise.
I'm proud, but also a bit intimidated by the stakes.
You're used to speaking in public, you'll do great.
I'll prepare my presentation carefully to be up to the task.
And above all, take the opportunity to meet experts in the field.
010: I'm thinking about starting my own business after all these years.
That's an ambitious project, but do you have a solid plan?
I have a clear idea and I've started researching the market.
That's a good foundation, but you'll also need to think about funding.
Yes, I'll consult an accountant to assess the feasibility.
That's wise, and don't hesitate to reach out to your network for advice.
